actions: Verified supplied reference video SHA-256 3781e4dcd3d21094f186cf442b3ee30cddfbb2fbe68d87c5c7470a2c742bf75a and candidate dist/index.html SHA-256 c4cc3c427fc52c9f91f6229c9aea0ae7cfe8220341be521df6c807626d101aae before inspection.
Extracted and visually inspected selected frames from the exact reference video (1100x720, 14.49646 fps, 36.49s); inspected source-video frame samples at 0s, 10s, 25s, and 30s plus a contact sheet.

Served candidate dist read-only on temporary localhost and stopped the server after testing. Used Playwright with fresh headless Chromium at 1100x720; normal mouse input only, no game/debug/state APIs.
Session 1: opened candidate, waited 1.5s, clicked viewport center once, waited 1.2s, held mouse 0.9s, moved 30px right over 0.5s, released, and waited 1s; saved observed screenshots.

Session 2: opened fresh candidate, waited 1s, clicked center once, clicked center 20 times at 300ms intervals, then waited 8s without input; saved screenshots after start, loop tap 8, loop tap 20, and idle 8s. Visible state reached stage 2 at distance 18 after loop taps; after idle it showed failure/score 38.
Observed a reference-vs-candidate visual presentation difference only; input traces are not paired and no requirement document was provided to classify it as a defect.

findings.observation: The sampled reference and observed candidate use visibly different course framing and HUD scale. In the recording, the knife appears small over a narrow elevated white route in an open green landscape; the candidate uses a much larger foreground cleaver, a broad route against large faceted hills, and prominent stage/score overlays.
findings.expectedVsObserved: Reference samples at 0s, 10s, 25s, and 30s show the narrow-route/distant-knife presentation and fruit/hazard progression; candidate fresh-start and ordinary-tap screenshots show the large-cleaver/broad-route/stage-HUD presentation. This documents a presentation difference, not a requirement violation or gameplay defect.
findings.uncertainty: The reference is recording-only with no input trace or synchronized timebase. No visual specification or approved adaptation target was supplied, so it is unknown whether this difference is intended; gameplay non-equivalence cannot be inferred from these screens.

gaps: The supplied reference has no input trace; click/tap cadence and actions cannot be paired with candidate inputs, so progression timing, obstacle avoidance, and terminal outcome are not comparable.

Reference playback samples show course progression to a checkered multiplier structure around 30s; the candidate normal-input sequence reached stage 2 at distance 18, then failed after 8s with no input. A candidate successful terminal/settlement was not observed.
Replay was not exercised. Only the specified 1100x720 viewport and two fresh candidate sessions were used; no mobile-size/orientation run was performed.
No user-facing requirements or verified expected behavior were supplied; this is a bounded qualitative observation, not release approval.
